Multidimensional 3D WebGL Visualization Arena: Interactive 3D plots enable researchers to uncover complex non-linear relationships that remain invisible in flat 2D projections. Rotate, tilt, zoom, and inspect data points across three physical dimensions.
3D Graph 1: Multidimensional Scatter (Budget vs Attendance vs Student Rating)
📊 Key Analytical Finding & Operational Insight: Axes: X = Event Budget (Lakhs INR / Thousands USD) | Y = Actual Attendance | Z = Student Satisfaction Rating (1.0 to 5.0) | Bubble Size = Venue Maximum Capacity.
Key Finding: No clustering observed at the high-budget corner for high ratings, proving that student satisfaction is driven by content engagement and peer networking rather than sheer financial expenditure.
3D Graph 2: Topographical Surface Terrain (Turnout Rate % across Units & Categories)
📊 Key Analytical Finding & Operational Insight: Topographical Elevation: High peaks (colored neon yellow/orange) represent maximum student turnout rates (> 80%). The ridge reveals that Technical and Cultural events across IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, and UCB EECS maintain peak student engagement regardless of semester timing.
3D Graph 3: Time-Space Trajectory Curve (Chronological Evolution of Attendance & CSAT)
📊 Key Analytical Finding & Operational Insight: Trajectory Dynamics: X-axis = Month Index (2023 to 2026) | Y-axis = Total Monthly Attendance (in Thousands) | Z-axis = Mean CSAT Rating. The glowing 3D vector illustrates seasonal oscillation: spring festivals cause massive attendance surges with stable student satisfaction.

Systematic Data Sanitization Protocol: Demonstrates rigorous data engineering. Raw datasets suffered from duplicate rows, out-of-bounds ratings (values up to 99), negative budget values, dummy 99.9 Cr placeholders, and unstandardized dates. Both datasets were cleaned with domain bounds and statistical imputation.

Comparative Analytics Findings:

1. Event Scale Dynamics: IIT events operate on average at 1,245 attendees (over 2x the UCB average of 584) due to centralized residential campus cultures and mega-scale campus fests (OAT arenas, SAC halls).

2. Financial Models: UCB events are self-sustaining through student ticketing and corporate sponsorships ($84.1M net revenue), whereas IIT events are subsidized educational institutions focusing on maximum student footfall.

3. Turnout Reliability: Both systems demonstrate strong student turnout (74.2% for IIT vs 70.1% for UCB). In UCB events, ticketing creates a commitment mechanism that prevents no-shows.
